Done — all 5 tests pass (`5 passed in 0.01s`).

What I changed:
- **`stats.py`** — added `median(xs)`: sorts a copy of the input, returns the middle element for odd-length input and the average of the two middle elements for even-length input. It raises `ValueError` on an empty sequence rather than leaking an `IndexError`, per your explicit-error-handling rule.
- **`test_stats.py`** — added three tests covering odd-length, even-length, and empty input, matching the existing test style. The two existing `mean` tests still pass.

Two environment notes from running the suite, neither related to this code:
- Your shell's default `python3` points at a venv from another project (`~/Desktop/Projects/hackathons/bob/.venv`) that has no pytest, so I used Homebrew's Python 3.14 instead.
- That Homebrew pytest crashes on startup because a globally installed `web3` package registers a pytest plugin that fails to import (`pkg_resources` missing). I worked around it with `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`; if you want pytest working normally again, `pip install setuptools` into `~/Library/Python/3.14` (or remove that stray `web3` install) would fix it.
